title: Release versions and checksums disagree
files: 05_release/README.md, SHA256SUMS.txt and seven DOCX; 01_templates/; 07_final_audit/corrected_docx/; specification and both delivery PDFs
problem: Seven of eight release DOCX fail their recorded SHA-256 values. Bilingual Continuation is the one matching file. The README says release files are identical to 01_templates, but seven are different. Later corrections exist only in 07_final_audit; the PDFs and specification still describe R1. A recipient cannot identify one reproducible version.
source: C document/release control; Register AC20; QA open gates VAL-16/VAL-21; local source-preservation and release records
correction: Select one controlled candidate after reconciling intentional owner edits with 07_final_audit corrections. Archive conflicting derivatives rather than deleting them. Generate every companion DOCX/PDF/specification from that same candidate; update README, manifest, change log and SHA256SUMS together. Do not merely replace checksums to conceal unsynchronized files.
acceptance: All delivery hashes verify; canonical/release copies agree; PDF/specification settings match selected DOCX. Preserve working status and AC20.
status: FAIL; later correction candidate available, package promotion incomplete
implemented_correction: Selected corrected baseline, retained useful release edits, regenerated all companions and synchronized release copies. Original variants archived in place, not overwritten.

title: Active typography no longer follows the approved font policy
problem: The fresh headless bilingual export uses TimesNewRomanPSMT for four bracket characters. Executive subject exports as Jost-Bold rather than the Regular 400 used in R1/corrected files. These are active rendering facts, not inferred from unused style definitions. Font substitution must not be accepted silently.
source: A typography, slides 34–35; B slides 9–12; Register L01/L04/L06/L08; user font-fallback rule
correction: Give entire Latin metadata tokens explicit Inter Regular in ascii/hAnsi/cs and LTR direction; remove inherited fallback mapping. Restore Executive subject to supplied Jost Regular 400 with w:b/w:bCs off. Use only verified in-use font builds. Reopen and export on the required Word platforms; stop on substitution or damaged glyphs.
acceptance: Every active exported text run uses Inter/Jost/Noto Sans Arabic as intended, with Regular 400 weight; no Times New Roman or silent fallback.
status: FAIL release render; corrected candidate passes the observed font-family check
implemented_correction: Inter LTR identifiers remain whole; Executive subject is Jost Regular; fresh exports use only Inter/Jost/Noto Regular. Specification theme-font inheritance also removed after the final check detected an unintended substitute. No active substitute or synthetic Bold observed. Native Word platform matrix pending.
revision_03_evidence: Native Word for Mac and LibreOffice exports use only Inter/Jost/Noto Sans Arabic Regular.

title: Arabic PDF text layer does not preserve the source text
files: 05_release/GEM_Letterhead_Digital.pdf and Print.pdf; 07_final_audit/evidence/word_renders/ Arabic and bilingual PDFs; fresh private exports of both DOCX families
page: Delivery portfolio pages 3–6; Arabic/bilingual first and continuation proofs
problem: Pypdf and pdfplumber independently expose damaged Arabic character mapping. The older Digital PDF inserts digit 7 into the Arabic contractual-disclaimer phrase and I into the signatory word. Word evidence PDFs replace dots/diacritics with symbols and digits. Fresh corrected exports also contain malformed extracted Arabic. Visual shaping can look correct while copy/paste, search and assistive reading lose the intended wording. This contradicts the earlier assumption that R1 Arabic extraction was fully correct.
source: Register V05/V13; B Arabic/localization mechanics and accessibility; qa/PartB_RC2_RTL_Localization_QA_Report.md; VAL-07/VAL-08/VAL-15
correction: Verify the font-to-Unicode mapping and export pipeline. Choose a renderer/font configuration that preserves logical Unicode Arabic, then regenerate both delivery portfolios and individual proofs. Compare complete normalized extracted text with the DOCX source; test punctuation, diacritics, recipient/signature strings and mixed IDs. Correct mapping/ActualText where required without flattening text into images.
owner: Document Accessibility QA and Arabic Lead
acceptance: Two independent extractors return source-equivalent Arabic; native copy/paste/search and Arabic assistive reading are tested. Tag presence and visual readability alone do not pass.
status: FAIL text-layer checks; localization/assistive acceptance remains PENDING
implemented_correction: Repaired omitted Arabic combining-mark ToUnicode entries from exporter ActualText, corrected base/mark cluster allocation, and preserved logical source paragraph ActualText. Pypdf layout and pdfplumber independently match the complete Arabic glyph inventory; semantic source paragraphs match DOCX. Generic plain extraction still reverses/omits mixed RTL fragments. This finding is not closed. Native copy/search and AT must pass before controlled real-world PDF use.
revision_03_result: FAIL (generic extractors) / PASS (native PDFKit copy-search) / PENDING (assistive technology)
revision_03_evidence: R03-02 corrected mixed-direction identifiers; all template lines pass native PDFKit copy/search; pypdf, poppler and pdfplumber still reorder/omit Arabic identically to Rev02.

title: Mixed-direction reference token breaks in the bilingual release
problem: The fresh render displays the reference as REFERENCE] on one line and [NUMBER on the next. Brackets fall outside their intended token order, and a short placeholder already wraps poorly. This is a usable-field defect, not a preference for one bilingual visual arrangement.
source: B slides 12–13: Latin technical IDs stay LTR and isolated; Register M05–M08; RTL QA
correction: Keep the complete reference field in a single LTR group with explicit Inter font and zero tracking, inside the RTL paragraph. Give it sufficient width; allow long references to wrap only in LTR order. Test actual emails, URLs, phone values and codes without inventing company details. Keep Arabic paragraph alignment and logo orientation unchanged.
acceptance: Short and long reference codes retain bracket/punctuation order; English identifiers, phone, email and URL remain LTR on one-, two- and three-page letters.
status: FAIL release render; corrected placeholder render is stable
implemented_correction: Separated date and reference into editable lines; full technical ID uses one explicit Inter LTR run. Short/long codes render in correct bracket order. Email/URL/phone test fields are fixtures only, never company details.
revision_03_evidence: Superseded by R03-02 after native Word and PDFKit evidence.

title: English first-page pagination exports incomplete text
page: Page 1 footer, including later-page conditional field behaviour
problem: The fresh bundled-renderer export shows Page of without page numbers. This file contains a nested IF/NUMPAGES/PAGE field construction; the corrected companion exports Page 1 of 1. Complex fields exist, so they must not be misreported as absent or ordinary typed text. The failure is verified in this export engine, not universally asserted for Microsoft Word.
source: C release/preflight discipline; local letterhead specification: live PAGE/NUMPAGES; Register W03/V13
correction: Use robust PAGE/NUMPAGES fields with consistent run formatting, or repair and separately validate the conditional expression if its hide-on-one-page behaviour is intentionally retained. Refresh fields before export and verify every page. Keep field results compatible with the selected renderer.
acceptance: No orphan Page of text. One-, two- and three-page Word/PDF outputs show correct numbers or intentionally suppress the whole label.
status: FAIL headless compatibility; native Word result PENDING
implemented_correction: Selected robust live PAGE/NUMPAGES fields with 9 pt Inter formatting. One-page templates and 2/3-page explicit/automatic-flow fixtures show correct page values in the bundled renderer. No incomplete Page of output.
revision_03_evidence: Correct Page i of N on every page of 43 native Word jobs.

title: Localization status does not travel with all continuation pages
files: 01_templates and 05_release Arabic/Bilingual First Page and Continuation DOCX; delivery Digital/Print pages 3–6
page: All automatic continuation pages and footer variants
problem: PENDING LOCALIZATION APPROVAL is in sample body text, but absent from the release footer variants. Once the sample body is replaced or a continuation page flows automatically, the localization gate can disappear. Later corrected candidates already carry the marker in all relevant footers.
source: Register AC10/AC20; B open-localization status; RTL QA; local pending-status discipline
correction: Carry the existing localization-status wording in first/default/even footers of every Arabic and bilingual candidate until Arabic approval is evidenced. Promote the proven footer correction consistently; do not treat sample-body wording as sufficient.
acceptance: Every Arabic/bilingual page retains the correct pending marker after sample replacement and multipage flow.
status: FAIL release coverage; PASS corrected structural/footer render
implemented_correction: Working and localization status retained in all first/default footers of Arabic and bilingual templates, including automatic continuations.
revision_03_evidence: Present on every native Word page.

title: Tagline size and tracking drift across release variants
files: 05_release/GEM_Letterhead_Executive.docx; English_First_Page.docx; Arabic/Bilingual first-page headers require style reconciliation
problem: Executive explicitly sets 8.5 pt with 38 twips expanded spacing: about 0.224em, rather than 0.18em, and below the 12 CSS px threshold at which tracking is permitted. The release English tagline lacks the explicit spacing run used in R1. R1/corrected first-page taglines consistently use 10.5 pt and 38 twips, approximately 0.181em.
source: Register B03/L09; A slides 23/36; B slides 10–11; local specification page 2
correction: Restore the controlled Jost Regular 10.5 pt tagline run with Word-quantized 38-twip tracking, or compute 0.18em for an explicitly approved size. Apply consistent spacing to the tagline only; keep all running and Arabic text at zero tracking.
acceptance: All retained taglines share the approved tracking treatment and the selected application size; no tracking below the digital threshold.
status: FAIL release drift; PASS corrected explicit settings
implemented_correction: Selected corrected Jost Regular tagline at 10.5 pt, 38 twips (~0.181em). Body and Arabic have zero expanded tracking.

title: Digital status and footer sizes lack a documented stationery exception
page: Footers/status; specification footer and source labels
problem: Delivery PDF uses 6.5 pt working-status text and 7.5 pt contact/footer text. Part B labelSmall is 12 CSS px (9 pt), with a 14 px caption style. These page-based application values are documented, but no stationery-specific digital exception or legibility evidence is approved. This is not a claim that Part B web-body sizing must be mechanically applied to A4 letters, or that 9 pt is a validated physical-print minimum.
source: B slide 10 and type tokens; C physical-size/process-test gates; Register accessibility and owner approval
correction: For digital use, test a status/footer treatment at 9 pt or higher and reflow only that zone if needed, or obtain an explicit application exception supported by legibility/accessibility evidence. Keep print minimums pending supplier/process proof; do not invent them.
owner: Accessibility QA, Brand Owner and Production Lead
acceptance: Approved application decision plus real digital/print legibility evidence; no tiny text carrying essential status without validation.
status: PENDING application validation; measured digital token mismatch
implemented_correction: Raised essential footer/status and SAMPLE CONTENT to 9 pt; footer explicitly 12.6 pt exact leading. Visual/grayscale review passed with no collision. This is a working digital application choice, not a newly approved stationery/physical minimum. Owner digital legibility and supplier print proof remain required.
revision_03_evidence: 9 pt meets the Part B labelSmall 12 px floor and is legible in native Word; owner acceptance, tracking token and physical proof remain.

title: Unexpected clipboard-like symbols appear in exports

page: After continuation-text placeholder; beside Executive SAMPLE CONTENT
problem: The fresh PDF proofs contain clipboard-like symbols that are absent from the R1 delivery portfolio and corrected candidate renders. No matching ordinary emoji text or body-picture record was found, so their exact source/export cause remains unconfirmed. They are visible unintended output artifacts, not asserted to be newly drawn GEM assets.
source: A restrained applications/composition; B functional-glyph consistency; C output preflight
correction: Trace the placeholder/content-control or export behaviour causing the symbols and remove them from the delivered output, preserving editable content. Use a verified output engine if the artifact is renderer-specific. Do not add new decorative iconography to compensate.
acceptance: No clipboard-like or other unintended symbol appears in native and PDF exports.
status: FAIL fresh export appearance; cause PENDING
implemented_correction: Selected clean editable corrected source and discarded corrupt release re-save structures while preserving originals. No unintended clipboard-like symbol appears in fresh exports. Exact original renderer/add-in cause is not asserted.
revision_03_evidence: No stray symbols in native Word or LibreOffice renders.

title: Release font embedding contains empty parts
page: Package fontTable relationships and embedded font payloads
problem: Each changed file carries four zero-byte font payloads referenced as Inter/Noto Sans Arabic variants; English First Page has a fifth zero-byte part. Files grew to roughly 6 MB and include many unused embedded variants. Empty files do not prove that every currently used Regular font is missing, but they are not valid embedded-font evidence. Active fallback is separately reported in LH02.
source: B font deployment/acceptance gate VAL-05; C manifest/handoff; official font/license record; local font manifest
correction: Embed only the required verified in-use Regular font builds, with nonempty decodable payloads and accurate relationships. Remove unused invalid references only after confirming they are not used. Preserve licensing and original font provenance; regenerate checksums after the controlled repair.
acceptance: All referenced embedded fonts decode and match the manifest; only intended active families/weights render; package size and embedding status are truthfully documented.
status: FAIL embedding integrity; active Regular-font absence not assumed
implemented_correction: Preserved three valid Regular-only font payloads from the corrected candidate. Every payload decoded as a usable TTF with cmap; decoded hashes recorded. No zero-byte embedded parts. Acceptance/licence gate remains open.
revision_03_evidence: Templates keep 3 valid Regular payloads; Word save behaviour corrected by R03-01.
